landmarks.name: Mills Memorial Library
facts: It is the main library for the humanities and social sciences.
The library moved into it in May 1951, paid for by a foundation set up by David Bloss ____.

landmarks.name: H.G. Thode Library of Science & Engineering
facts: It is named after a nuclear chemist who was the university's president.
It opened in 1978, replacing the first science library, a room in the Burke Science Building.

landmarks.name: Brandon Hall
facts: It houses the university's substance-free residence floors.

landmarks.name: Les Prince Hall
facts: It is a large co-ed residence that opened in 2006.

landmarks.name: Whidden Hall
facts: It is named after a former chancellor of the university.

landmarks.name: Lincoln Alexander Hall
facts: It is named after the first Black member of Canada's House of Commons.

landmarks.name: Peter George Centre for Living and Learning
facts: It is named after a former president of the university.
It was completed in fall 2019.

landmarks.name: McMaster Divinity College
facts: It traces its origins to the Toronto Baptist College.
In 1957 the university became a secular public institution, and its theology program became this separately chartered college.

landmarks.name: Arthur Bourns Building
facts: It is named after a former president of the university who was a chemist.

landmarks.name: Burke Science Building
facts: The university's first science library opened in a room here in 1954 and stayed until 1978.

landmarks.name: Life Sciences Building
facts: A new greenhouse was built in front of it in 2025.

landmarks.name: John Hodgins Engineering Building
facts: It is named after the university's first dean of engineering.

landmarks.name: Information Technology Building
facts: It is home to the Department of Computing and Software and to Electrical and Computer Engineering.

landmarks.name: Togo Salmon Hall
facts: In 1967, the university's art gallery was given a purpose-built space in its east wing.

landmarks.name: Gilmour Hall
facts: It houses the offices of the president and the registrar.

landmarks.name: DeGroote School of Business
facts: Its MBA program began in 1962, and a co-op option was added in 1973.

landmarks.name: Michael G. DeGroote Centre for Learning and Discovery
facts: It was built in 2004 and houses the medical school together with the adjacent Health Sciences Centre.

landmarks.name: Gerald Hatch Centre
facts: It was built for hands-on, experiential engineering learning and opened in 2017.

landmarks.name: McLean Centre for Collaborative Discovery
facts: It opened for occupancy in fall 2025.

landmarks.name: McMaster Nuclear Reactor
facts: It produces medical isotopes such as iodine-125.
When it started up in 1959, it was the first research facility of its kind at a university in the Commonwealth.

landmarks.name: University Hall
facts: It is one of the university's five original buildings in Hamilton.
When the university moved to Hamilton in 1930, the library was housed here.

landmarks.name: Hamilton Hall
facts: It is one of the original Collegiate Gothic buildings designed by William Lyon Somerville.
It opened in 1926 and is one of the oldest buildings on campus.

landmarks.name: Refectory
facts: Like University Hall and Hamilton Hall, it was designed by William Lyon Somerville in the Collegiate Gothic style.

landmarks.name: McMaster Museum of Art
facts: Its collection began with portraits of the university's presidents and faculty.
It opened to the public in its present location on June 11, 1994.

landmarks.name: Bertrand Russell Archives and Research Centre
facts: It holds the papers of a famous British philosopher.
It opened on June 25, 2018.

landmarks.name: David Braley Athletic Centre
facts: Students support it through a membership fee included in their student union fees.
Named after a former Canadian senator, it opened in 2007.

landmarks.name: Ron Joyce Stadium
facts: The Hamilton Tiger-Cats began their 2014 season here while Tim Hortons Field was being finished.
The 6,000-seat stadium opened in 2007.
